1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Modal/Modal.js – This is where componentDidUpdate adds and removes the `${prefix}--body--no-scroll` class from document.body when the Modal opens and closes. The logic is correct, but without CSS it has no effect.

2. packages/components/src/components/modal/modal.scss – This is the SCSS for the vanilla (CSS/JS) Modal component. We need to add styles here (or to a global place) for `.bx--body--no-scroll { overflow: hidden; }` (or whatever the prefix is) so that adding the class actually disables scrolling.

3. packages/react/src/components/Modal/Modal.test.js – Since we’re adding behavior around the body class, we should update or add tests here to verify that opening the Modal adds the class on document.body and closing removes it.

4. packages/react/src/components/ComposedModal/ComposedModal.js – The ComposedModal is a higher-level wrapper around Modal, and it currently doesn’t duplicate the body‐scroll disabling logic. If you want ComposedModal to prevent background scroll as well, you must ensure that it also passes an “open” prop into Modal (which it already does) so that the same class is applied. If any behavior is special in ComposedModal (e.g. different mounting container), you may need to mirror or enhance the logic here as well.
1.bug_scenario: When you open a transactional or passive Modal, you expect the background page (the <body>) to stop scrolling so that the user can’t scroll “under” the overlay. In the GIF you can see that although the Modal componentLogic in Modal.js is already attempting to disable scrolling by adding a “no-scroll” class to the document.body, there is no corresponding CSS rule shipped to actually prevent overflow. As a result the page continues to scroll while the Modal is open.

2.explanation: 1. packages/react/src/components/Modal/Modal.js: This is where the React Modal adds and removes the “${prefix}--body--no-scroll” class on document.body in componentDidUpdate. The class is never effectively preventing scroll (CSS for it is missing or mis-scoped), so body scrolling still happens. 2. packages/react/src/components/ModalWrapper/ModalWrapper.js: Although this wrapper only toggles open/close state, it is the entry point in React apps for displaying the modal. It uses the Modal above but does not itself enforce any scroll disabling—so it is indirectly involved in the broken workflow. 3. packages/components/src/components/modal/modal.js: This is the vanilla (non‐React) implementation of the modal used by the Carbon Components bundle. It contains no logic to disable or lock body scrolling when open, so users of the plain JS/SCSS bundle never get a scroll‐locked background either. You will need to add or correct the CSS rule for the no‐scroll class in your global SCSS and/or add the same class logic to this vanilla JS module so it matches the React component’s intent.
2.bug_scenario: In both the React‐based Carbon Modal (ModalWrapper → Modal) and the underlying vanilla JS/SCSS system, when you open a Transactional or Passive modal the page’s <body> remains scrollable. The user can still scroll the background content even though the modal is in front, which is not the expected “trap” behavior. In the React version there is code attempting to add a “no‐scroll” class to the <body> but in practice the scroll isn’t disabled (either because the CSS rule is missing, mis-named, or never shipped). The core vanilla modal in components/src/components/modal/modal.js likewise never disables background scrolling.
